parsed.explanation: Combined federal, state/provincial and municipal regime exposes trans adults and minors to passport/visa refusal, fraud/lifetime ineligibility, government-facility exclusion, hostile immigration/corrections custody with hormone removal and sexual abuse, and counterterrorism threat framing. The division adds severe restroom ordinance, birth-sex jail/search, and charging victims after violence. Existing legal challenges and some local protections are partial and not documented as overriding active federal border/facility/custody practice. No execution-level certainty, so not 0.05; severe universal institutional targeting places it in low-severe risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport/visa rules reflect assigned sex; 'X' barred. Discrepancies can cause refusal, additional evidence, fraud/lifetime ineligibility; passports blocked, travelers stranded; border advisory climate.
entry_documents.protection: Existing 'X' passports remain valid until expiry; litigation and legal-aid guidance.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal document mismatch feeds visa fraud screening, detention, and state/local facility or ID checks.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Corrections adopts conversion practices: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric therapy/drugs; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; division jailed trans woman in men's facility and male-searched despite female marker.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some federal policies enjoined; national hate-crime recourse; no documented effective custody remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy or local restroom confrontation can become fraud/immigration or criminal custody under birth-sex placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National EO bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; many state/provinces have bans; one municipality passed severe restroom ordinance; arrest for willful restroom use and refusal to depart; held in opposite-sex ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Many state/provinces lack mapped bans; some municipal anti-discrimination orders; not displace federal/state facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule plus state/local bans create broad public restroom exposure; private settings uneven.

care_services.exposure: Federal directives criminalize facilitating social transition and proposed minor care restrictions; division bans puberty blockers, hormones, surgery; crisis youth services removed; custody removes medication.
care_services.protection: Some orders blocked/enjoined; no documented operational travel-care shield.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking adult/minor or parent can trigger investigation or denial; detention medication interruption compounds risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism prioritizes identifying/neutralizing radical pro-transgender groups; gender ideology framed with violence; law enforcement directed to prosecute teachers facilitating social transition; local police charged victims after mob beating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Document states counterterrorism not used for mere disagreement; hate-crime and employment protections remain on books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing lowers reporting protection and increases security/document scrutiny; hostile local enforcement compounds.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders direct investigation/prosecution for facilitating social transition; minors' care banned in many places; schools/funding targeted; division bans care; guardians may face criminal exposure.
minors_guardians.protection: Some injunctions; legal-aid guidance; no documented protective regime for travelling families.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adult with trans minor faces document, school, facility, care, and possible guardian investigation at every stage.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Div: mob beat trans couple over restroom; victims charged, attacker not arrested; one denied hospital and jailed in men's facility; killings reported high but undercounted.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Municipal anti-discrimination ordinances and national hate-crime statute exist; plea/outcomes unresolved.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence becomes state exposure through charges and birth-sex custody rather than protected victim.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved litigation, partial injunctions; private-setting coverage and some custody/care unknown; undercounted killings; no documented effective relief for passport, facility, immigration custody.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU suit, legal FAQ, state/municipal protections, courts; not shown to override active federal border/custody rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Patchwork remedies are unpredictable and local, while federal entry, funding, and custody operate nationwide.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable severe state custody abuse and official threat. Rated slightly below 0.15-A because national passport/visa fraud, federal facility ban, immigration sexual abuse/forced labour and counterterrorism framing widen traveler-facing exposure; above 0.05 because execution not documented.

Much lower. Veluna has universal facility exclusion and polite street life; here document/visa fraud, immigration custody abuse, threat framing and division victim-charging make severity and probability of harmful discovery far higher.
Far lower than local ferry/guesthouse hostility with mediators; operative federal document/custody rules and official counterterrorism framing cannot be offset by local remedies.

parsed.synthesis: Federal entry/documents, facility rules and custody practices interact with state/local ordinances and police conduct. A passport marker mismatch can produce visa refusal, fraud finding, or detention; once detained, federal/state custody imposes birth-sex placement, hormone removal and reported sexual abuse. Restroom or public-space exposure can lead to criminal trespass arrest and male-search, while counterterrorism rhetoric legitimizes surveillance and reduces protective policing. Legal challenges and municipal protections create exceptions but are not documented as overriding the operative national regime, especially for minors and travelling guardians.
